*Note: This section covers the key operative provisions of the GX-ETS as described in the ICAP factsheet (the most detailed regulatory-level source available in the corpus). The primary enacted text (GX Promotion Act, implementing regulations) is referenced by name in the corpus sources but its full text is not reproduced in the source corpus provided. Section analysis therefore relies on the ICAP factsheet and the ANRE/METI GX Policy article as the closest available secondary-primary sources. Where the full text is needed, this is noted as a research gap.*

## Sectoral Coverage and Thresholds

The GX-ETS mandatory phase covers "all sectors" with an inclusion threshold of "companies with annual CO₂ emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more in power, industry, transport and aviation as well as in other sectors if their annual CO₂ emissions exceed the 100,000 tonnes threshold." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Specific definition of "company" for threshold-counting purposes (i.e., whether it is per legal entity, per facility, or per group) not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

## Allocation Methodology

*Analytical inference:* Phase 2 (FY2026–FY2032) uses free allocation with two methods:
- **Benchmarking** applies to: "Freight automobile transportation," "Domestic marine transportation," and "Air transportation," among 20 named product/sector categories. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets
- **Grandparenting** applies to sectors not specifically named in the benchmarking list. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* Benchmarking, by its nature, rewards more efficient operators with surplus allowances and penalises less efficient operators with shortfalls — creating competitive incentive within the road, marine, and air carrier sectors to reduce emissions intensity per unit of transport output.

## Price Stabilisation Mechanism

The scheme operates with both upper and lower price limits:
- "Upper price limit in FY2027: JPY 4,300 (USD 28.73). When allowance prices rise above an established upper price limit, entities can meet their obligations by paying the upper limit." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets
- "Lower price limit in FY2027: JPY 1,700 (USD 11.36). When a certain number of days pass with trading prices below the lower limit, a reverse auction will be held to balance the supply and demand for allowances." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Specific price limits for FY2026 (the current fiscal year) not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14; the figures above are stated for FY2027.*

## Compliance and Surrender Requirement

"Covered entities must surrender one compliance unit per tCO₂ that exceeds the facility's annual emissions limit." Compliance period is one year. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## Auctioning Introduction

*Analytical inference:* "From FY2033, auctioning will be introduced for high-emitting corporations in the power sector." The ICAP factsheet states auctioning revenues for power generation companies, together with revenues from the fossil fuel surcharge, will be used to redeem GX Economic Transition Bonds. The timing and scope of auctioning for transport sector entities beyond FY2033 is not specified in the corpus sources.

*Specific date for introduction of auctioning to transport-sector carriers not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

## GX Economy Transition Bonds

"The government will issue GX Economy Transition Bonds to provide support in the order of 20 trillion yen for advance investment by the private sector over the coming ten years." *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating logistics infrastructure or considering fleet or equipment investment in Japan, the GX Economy Transition Bonds programme represents a potential public financing mechanism. Eligibility criteria for freight-sector private entities are not specified in the corpus.

## Banking and Borrowing

*Analytical inference:* "Banking: There are currently no regulations for banking in place, but the government is examining the possibility of implementing banking rules in FY2027. Borrowing is not allowed." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## MRV Framework

Regulatory framework for MRV: GX Promotion Act. "Covered entities must submit their emissions reports annually by January 31 of the year following the reporting year. Emissions reports require third-party verification by an accredited verifier." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

---

## Carrier Data Acquisition — Japan Domestic Legs

Scope: All Japan domestic transport legs (road, domestic air, coastal marine) where carrier partners are or may be GX-ETS covered entities.

Gap from current operational baseline: *Analytical inference:* Most freight forwarding operations do not currently hold granular carrier-level CO₂ data for Japan domestic legs sufficient to meet GX-ETS-standard activity-based emissions accounting. The January 31 annual MRV submission deadline means verified carrier data will lag the reporting period.

Action: Negotiate carrier data-sharing clauses in Japan carrier contracts requiring provision of GX-ETS-verified annual emissions data or interim activity data by agreed dates.

## Allowance Cost Pass-Through — Contract Clause Review

Scope: All Japan-leg freight contracts with road, domestic air, and coastal marine carriers that may become (or are already) GX-ETS covered entities.

*Operational implication:* As GX-ETS allowance costs emerge in FY2026 and the GX-Surcharge enters in FY2028, carriers will seek to recover costs through rate adjustments or new surcharge line items. Contracts without explicit carbon cost pass-through provisions or rate review clauses leave the workspace exposed to unilateral mid-term cost increases.

Action: Commission a review of Japan carrier contract terms for carbon cost pass-through language within 60 days.

## Sub-National ETS Compliance Check — Tokyo and Saitama Facilities

Scope: Any logistics or warehouse facilities the workspace operates or procures within Tokyo metropolitan and Saitama prefectural boundaries.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether facility operators within Tokyo and Saitama are independently subject to the sub-national ETS cap-and-trade programmes requires legal review against the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's cap-and-trade programme and the Saitama Prefecture scheme.

## Offset Procurement Infrastructure — J-Credits and JCM

Scope: Applicable if the workspace or a carrier partner uses offset credits to meet up to 10% of GX-ETS compliance obligation.

*Operational implication:* J-Credits and JCM credits are administered jointly by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of the Environment. Procurement of these credits requires engagement with the J-Credit Scheme or JCM bilateral mechanisms. Lead times for credit procurement and registration are not specified in the corpus.

---

## Voluntary Phase Participation (Phase 1: FY2023–FY2025) — Now Closed

*Analytical inference:* The voluntary phase "spanning FY2023 and FY2025" concluded. "More than 700 companies, accounting for over 50% of national GHG emissions, participated in the voluntary ETS." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* Carriers that participated in the voluntary phase will have established MRV processes and allowance management infrastructure. Carriers that did not participate in the voluntary phase and now fall within mandatory scope face a steeper implementation transition in FY2026.

## Entities Below the 100,000 tCO₂ Threshold

Entities below the mandatory inclusion threshold are not obligated under the GX-ETS. "Companies with annual CO₂ emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more." Entities below this level fall outside the mandatory scheme. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* Smaller domestic Japanese haulage providers or niche domestic air operators may fall below the threshold and therefore be excluded from the mandatory GX-ETS. However, they remain subject to the existing carbon tax on fossil fuel use and, from FY2028, to the upstream GX-Surcharge as embedded in fuel costs.

## International vs. Domestic Transport Scope

The GX-ETS sectoral coverage for transport covers **Domestic Aviation** and **Transport** (road freight automobile transportation and domestic marine transportation). International aviation is listed separately under the ICAP sectoral coverage table alongside "Maritime." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether international ocean or air freight legs (as distinct from Japan domestic segments) are within the GX-ETS scope for carrier compliance purposes, and how the boundary between domestic and international transport is drawn for threshold and allocation purposes, requires legal review of the GX Promotion Act and implementing METI guidance.

*Analytical inference:* ## S1: Mandatory Participation (Phase 2, from FY2026)

The GX-ETS transitioned to a mandatory system in April 2026, covering transport, power, industry, and maritime sectors. "In the FY2026, which started in April 2026, the GX-ETS transitioned to a mandatory baseline-and-credit system." The inclusion threshold: "Companies with annual CO₂ emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more." Estimated mandatory-phase participants: "300–400 entities." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## S2: Emissions Cap (Bottom-Up Absolute Cap)

*Analytical inference:* "A bottom-up absolute cap limits the total emissions allowed in the system and is fixed ex-ante." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Specific cap quantity for the transport sector not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

## S3: Allowance Surrender Requirement

"Covered entities must surrender one compliance unit per tCO₂ that exceeds the facility's annual emissions limit." Compliance period: one year. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## S4: Free Allocation — Transport Sectors

Phase 2 free allocation applies with benchmarking for the following transport categories explicitly named:
- "Freight automobile transportation"
- "Domestic marine transportation"
- "Air transportation"

Grandparenting applies to sectors not listed in the benchmarking schedule. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Specific benchmark values (per tonne-km or other unit basis) for freight automobile transportation, domestic marine transportation, and air transportation not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

*Analytical inference:* ## S5: Price Corridor — Upper and Lower Limits

"Upper and lower price limits apply." For FY2027: upper JPY 4,300 (USD 28.73), lower JPY 1,700 (USD 11.36). When the upper limit is breached, entities may discharge obligations by paying that limit. When prices remain below the lower limit for a sustained period, a reverse auction is held. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* The price corridor constrains the maximum allowance cost exposure for transport carriers in FY2027 at JPY 4,300/tCO₂. At current Japan road and domestic air emission intensities, this provides a calculable worst-case surcharge per tonne-kilometre, though the per-shipment cost depends on emission intensity data that must be sourced from individual carrier reporting.

## S6: Offset Credits (Phase 2)

- Eligible credits: Domestic J-Credits and international JCM credits (from 31 JCM partner countries).
- Quantitative limit: capped at 10% of an entity's compliance obligation.
- Qualitative requirement: credits are sourced from eligible programmes only. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## S7: MRV and Annual Reporting

- Framework: GX Promotion Act.
- Covered entities submit annual emissions reports by January 31 of the year following the reporting year.
- Third-party verification by an accredited verifier is required. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## S8: GX-Surcharge (from FY2028)

"A fossil fuel surcharge will be introduced from FY2028. It will be imposed on importers of fossil fuels at the time of importation in proportion to their carbon emissions when they are used." This is levied on fuel importers upstream of the transport carrier. *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

*Specific surcharge rate per tonne of CO₂ not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

## S9: Penalty Provision

**Penalty summary slot (FACT):** "If the required number of allowances cannot be surrendered, a payment equal to the shortfall in emission allowances × upper price × 1.1 must be made." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* At FY2027 price limits, the penalty rate for a one-tonne shortfall is JPY 4,300 × 1.1 = JPY 4,730/tCO₂ (approximately USD 31.60). For transport sector entities with large shortfalls, this could represent material financial exposure. The workspace should ensure any Japan carrier partner subject to GX-ETS has a credible allowance management plan in order to avoid financial distress that might affect service reliability.

## S10: NDC and Long-Term Target Context

*Analytical inference:* Japan's GHG reduction targets: "By FY2030: 46% reduction from FY2013 GHG levels, including LULUCF credits; and continue efforts to cut emissions by 50% (NDC 1.0). By 2050: Net zero GHG emissions (NDC 2.0)." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* The 46%–50% by FY2030 national target implies a trajectory of tightening caps and/or increasing carbon pricing across the GX instrument suite over the next four fiscal years, creating a structural cost-increase trend for fossil-fuel-dependent Japan domestic transport.

---

## MRV Registration and Reporting (Obligated Entities)

Obligated entities (those exceeding 100,000 tCO₂/year) are covered under the GX Promotion Act MRV framework. "Covered entities must submit their emissions reports annually by January 31 of the year following the reporting year. Emissions reports require third-party verification by an accredited verifier." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in its freight forwarding or logistics role on Japan trade lanes, is required to register under the GX Promotion Act as a covered entity, and what the registration mechanism entails (including the administering METI process), requires confirmation from Japan-qualified legal counsel.

## GX Acceleration Agency (GXA) — Operational Registration Hub

The GXA is "established to carry out operations related to the ETS and the GX-Surcharge system." It is the operational hub for ETS participation and surcharge administration. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Specific GXA registration portal, format, and filing requirements for transport-sector entities not available from primary sources as of 2026-07-14.*

## Sub-National ETS — Tokyo and Saitama

Japan operates two sub-national ETS schemes: "Sub-national ETSs: in Tokyo and Saitama." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether workspaces operating logistics or warehousing facilities within Tokyo or Saitama face separate sub-national ETS registration and reporting obligations, distinct from GX-ETS, requires legal review of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and Saitama Prefecture cap-and-trade programmes. The corpus does not contain the sub-national scheme texts.

## Carrier-Level Emissions Data — Scope 3 Reporting Interface

*Operational implication:* For workspaces using carrier data for Scope 3 or client sustainability reporting, the GX-ETS annual MRV cycle means Japan-leg carrier emissions data will be verified annually with a January 31 submission date. Data covering the prior calendar/fiscal year may not be available in verified form until after that date. Workspaces should negotiate data-sharing provisions with Japan carrier partners as part of standard commercial agreements.

---

The GX-ETS compliance chain in the transport sector operates at the level of individual companies whose annual CO₂ emissions exceed 100,000 tonnes. "The emissions trading system targets companies whose CO₂ emissions exceed a certain threshold. The Government will allocate free allowances to target companies, and they will trade any excess or shortfall in allowances on the market." *Source: Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ANRE), METI — GX Policy article, ANRE/METI, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

The compliance chain for a freight forwarding workspace on Japan trade lanes likely has the following structure:

- **Tier 1 — Obligated carriers:** Road freight operators ("Freight automobile transportation"), domestic maritime operators ("Domestic marine transportation"), and air carriers ("Air transportation") whose emissions exceed the threshold are directly covered by the mandatory GX-ETS Phase 2. Free allocation is assigned via benchmarking for these named sectors. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets
- **Tier 2 — Cost pass-through:** *Analytical inference:* Obligated carriers facing allowance shortfalls or purchasing allowances on the market are likely to recover those costs through freight rate adjustments or fuel/environmental surcharges on Japan domestic segments. Workspaces procuring domestic Japan haulage or domestic air or coastal marine legs will encounter these cost structures.
- **Tier 3 — International freight forwarder / NVOCC:** *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a freight forwarding workspace acting in a principal or agent capacity on Japan-origin or Japan-destination freight is itself classified as an obligated entity under the GX Promotion Act, or whether its position in the compliance chain is limited to commercial cost absorption and voluntary/client-driven reporting, requires Japan-qualified legal counsel review.

The GX Acceleration Agency (GXA) is the operational hub: "Established to carry out operations related to the ETS and the GX-Surcharge system." It "will provide debt guarantees for GX projects, operate the ETS, and administer the fossil fuel surcharge." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

---

## Q1: Does the workspace itself meet the 100,000 tCO₂ threshold for mandatory GX-ETS inclusion?

**Status:** *Legal Confirmation Required.* The threshold is defined as "companies with annual CO₂ emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more." Whether the workspace's Japan-origin and Japan-destination freight activities, combined across Scope 1 and attributed Scope 3 emissions (if either basis is used for threshold calculation), meet this level requires legal and operational assessment against the GX Promotion Act's definitions. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## Q2: Do Japan-leg carrier partners fall within the mandatory GX-ETS scope?

**Status:** Partially determinable from available sources. The GX-ETS explicitly covers "Freight automobile transportation," "Domestic marine transportation," and "Air transportation" sectors in Phase 2. Whether a specific carrier partner meets the 100,000 tCO₂ individual company threshold is carrier-specific and not determinable from the corpus. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

Recommended action: Request GX-ETS registration status confirmation from each Japan-leg carrier partner.

## Q3: Is borrowing of allowances permitted for transport-sector entities that face a shortfall?

*Analytical inference:* **Status:** FACT — borrowing is not allowed under the GX-ETS. "Borrowing is not allowed." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## Q4: Can J-Credits or JCM credits substitute for the full compliance obligation?

**Status:** FACT — quantitative cap applies. "The use of offset credits is capped at 10% of an entity's compliance obligation." J-Credits (domestic) and JCM credits (international, from 31 partner countries) are eligible. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## Q5: Is the GX-ETS linked to non-Japanese carbon markets?

*Analytical inference:* **Status:** FACT — no linking. "The GX-ETS will not be linked with any other system." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that hold carbon credits or allowances from the EU ETS, CORSIA, or other systems cannot use those instruments for GX-ETS compliance. Japan operates a fully siloed compliance instrument.

## The GX Framework in Plain Language

Japan's Green Transformation (GX) policy is a multi-instrument national strategy aimed at simultaneously achieving decarbonisation, energy security, and economic growth. The primary enacted instrument is the **GX Promotion Act** (formally the "Act on Promoting Transition to a Decarbonized Growth Economic Structure"), enacted in 2023. An amending act — the "Amended GX Promotion Act" — was adopted by the Upper House of the Parliament in May 2025, establishing the mandatory phase of the GX-ETS. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

The framework combines three carbon pricing instruments:

*Analytical inference:* 1. **An existing carbon tax** — "Tax for Climate Change Mitigation on fossil fuels since 2012." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets
2. **The GX-ETS** — a baseline-and-credit emissions trading scheme. "Japan started its GX-ETS as a voluntary baseline-and-credit system during its first phase spanning FY2023 and FY2025. In the FY2026, which started in April 2026, the GX-ETS transitioned to a mandatory baseline-and-credit system." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets
3. **The GX-Surcharge** — "a carbon levy (GX-Surcharge) to be introduced from 2028 on fossil fuel importers and domestic fossil fuel extractors." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* The overarching financial ambition: "The GX Promotion Strategy aims to spur up JPY150 trillion (USD 1 trillion) of public and private sector investment over the next 10 years." *Source: Amundi Research Center — Japan Green Transformation: a bold ambition, Amundi, 30 July 2025. https://research-center.amundi.com/article/japan-green-transformation-bold-ambition-speed-transition-asia

## Why It Applies to Freight Forwarding Operations

The GX-ETS in its mandatory phase (FY2026 onwards) covers transport as one of its enumerated sectors. The sectoral coverage explicitly includes **Transport** and **Domestic Aviation**, in addition to Industry, Power, and Maritime. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

Inclusion thresholds: "Companies with annual CO₂ emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more in power, industry, transport and aviation as well as in other sectors if their annual CO₂ emissions exceed the 100,000 tonnes threshold." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a freight forwarding workspace, depending on its specific operational role in Japan (carrier, agent, NVOCC, or freight forwarder), meets the defined obligated-entity threshold of 100,000 tCO₂/year under the GX-ETS, and whether any compliance obligation attaches directly to that entity or only to the carrier it engages, requires legal review against the GX Promotion Act and implementing regulations.

Additionally, under the GX-ETS in its mandatory phase, transport sector entities falling under the inclusion threshold are subject to free allocation methods (benchmarking for freight automobile transportation and domestic marine transportation and air transportation). *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

**Effective date slot (FACT):** The mandatory GX-ETS phase began in April 2026. "The mandatory GX-ETS began in April 2026, following a three-year voluntary phase and the adoption of the 'Amended GX Promotion Act' by the Upper House of the Parliament in May 2025." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

**Jurisdictional scope slot (FACT):** The GX-ETS applies in Japan, covering Japanese national GHG emissions. The scheme covers entities "accounting for over 50% of national GHG emissions" across all sectors. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

This document covers Japan's Green Transformation (GX) policy framework as it applies to freight transport operations, focusing on the GX Promotion Act (enacted 2023), the GX-ETS (Emissions Trading Scheme), the forthcoming GX-Surcharge on fossil fuels (FY2028), and the GX Economy Transition Bonds programme. It synthesises the regulatory corpus available from the sources provided and applies those findings to workspaces operating in freight forwarding and logistics roles on air-primary, road-secondary, and ocean-tertiary trade lanes touching Japan.

**Convention notes:**

- "FY" denotes Japan's fiscal year, which runs April 1 – March 31. FY2026 began April 1, 2026.
- Monetary figures appear in JPY and USD (approximate, as used in source material).
- All FACT citations are grounded to verbatim spans from the SOURCE corpus blocks.
- ANALYSIS claims are prefixed with the closed-label tokens "Analytical inference:", "Industry interpretation:", or "Operational implication:".

## MONITORING — Assess Threshold Exposure Against the 100,000 tCO₂ Inclusion Threshold

Assess, within 30 days, whether Japan-based operations or Japan-touching carrier contracts generate aggregate annual CO₂ emissions at or approaching the 100,000 tCO₂ mandatory GX-ETS inclusion threshold.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces whose Japan-origin or Japan-destination freight involves carriers that are themselves GX-ETS obligated entities may face indirect cost exposure as those carriers pass through allowance costs — independent of whether the workspace itself meets the threshold directly. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in its role as freight forwarder or NVOCC, is independently treated as an obligated entity under the GX-ETS framework, or whether its obligations are confined to its position as a shipper or cargo principal requiring carrier-side compliance, must be confirmed with Japan-qualified legal counsel reviewing the GX Promotion Act and implementing Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) guidance.

## MONITORING — Map Carrier Pass-Through Risk for the GX-Surcharge (FY2028)

Map, within 60 days, which Japan-leg carrier contracts (road haulage, domestic air, domestic marine) are not currently locked on fuel surcharges beyond FY2028.

*Operational implication:* The GX-Surcharge, described as "a carbon levy to be introduced from 2028 on fossil fuel importers and domestic fossil fuel extractors," is expected to raise the cost base for transport fuel in Japan beginning FY2028. Carriers facing higher fuel input costs are likely to introduce or increase fuel surcharges on Japan domestic freight segments. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## MONITORING — Track MRV Reporting Infrastructure Requirement (Annual Deadline: January 31)

Verify, within 30 days, whether any Japan-operation carrier partner or affiliated entity falls within GX-ETS mandatory scope and whether the workspace's existing emissions reporting infrastructure can receive and process the required carrier-level activity data.

*Operational implication:* "Covered entities must submit their emissions reports annually by January 31 of the year following the reporting year. Emissions reports require third-party verification by an accredited verifier." For workspaces that aggregate carrier data for Scope 3 or client sustainability reporting purposes, data latency on Japan transport legs may affect annual reporting timelines. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

## MONITORING — Engage on Offset Credit Eligibility (J-Credits and JCM Credits)

Engage with Japan-specialist sustainability advisors within 60 days to understand whether J-Credit or JCM-credit procurement is feasible to offset Japan-leg transport emissions at the workspace or shipper level.

*Operational implication:* "The use of offset credits is allowed [in Phase 2]. Domestic (J-Credits) and international (JCM credits) credits are allowed with quantitative limits. The use of offset credits is capped at 10% of an entity's compliance obligation." This cap means offset credits alone cannot substitute for structural emissions reduction on high-emission Japan transport lanes. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

**Primary deadline slot (FACT):** The closest primary compliance deadline is the annual emissions report submission date of January 31 following each reporting year, under the GX Promotion Act MRV framework, applicable to covered entities from FY2026 onwards. *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

---

## MONITORING — FY2027 Banking Rule Decision

*Analytical inference:* The government is examining the possibility of implementing banking rules in FY2027. This is a FACT as stated: "the government is examining the possibility of implementing banking rules in FY2027." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* If banking rules are introduced in FY2027, covered entities in the transport sector could carry surplus allowances into future compliance periods, reducing price volatility risk and enabling more strategic investment in emissions reduction over a multi-year horizon. The workspace should re-check this status in Q1 FY2027 (April–June 2026 for Japan-facing analysis).

## MONITORING — GX-Surcharge (FY2028 Introduction)

"A fossil fuel surcharge will be introduced from FY2028. It will be imposed on importers of fossil fuels at the time of importation in proportion to their carbon emissions when they are used." *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

The ICAP factsheet confirms: "GX-Surcharge on fuel imports and domestic extractors (upcoming, FY2028)." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

Implementing regulations for the GX-Surcharge rate and calculation methodology are not yet published in the corpus sources. The workspace should monitor METI publications from mid-FY2027 onwards for rate-setting consultations.

## MONITORING — Mandatory GX-ETS Benchmarks and Grandfathering (Stakeholder Consultation Through 2025)

*Analytical inference:* "Over the course of 2025, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) held several working group meetings to consult stakeholders on various design aspects of the mandatory GX-ETS such as benchmarks and grandfathering for setting the baselines and upper and lower price limits of emission allowances." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* Final benchmarks for freight automobile transportation, domestic marine transportation, and air transportation are the key unknowns determining how many allowances will be freely allocated to transport carriers. These benchmarks, once published by METI, will determine whether obligated carriers are in surplus or shortfall, directly affecting the degree to which allowance costs are passed through to freight rates.

## MONITORING — GX2040 Vision Implementation

The GX2040 Vision was approved by the Cabinet in February 2025 alongside the 7th Strategic Energy Plan. "In February 2025, the Cabinet approved the 7th Strategic Energy Plan, along with the GX2040 Vision as a national strategy to show the prospects for advancing GX and related support measures." *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

The GX2040 Vision establishes the long-term industrial cluster and location strategy but does not itself impose immediate freight-sector compliance deadlines beyond those already operative under the GX Promotion Act. Re-check window: FY2026 sector-specific implementing measures under the GX2040 Vision.

## MONITORING — Urban Green Space Act and Urban Logistics Interfaces (May 2024 Amendment)

The Urban Green Space Act was partially amended in May 2024 and includes green infrastructure requirements that may intersect with urban freight terminal and warehouse location planning in Japanese cities. "For sustainable urban development, the act was partially amended in May 2024." *Source: MLIT City Bureau — Green Transformation for Sustainable Urban Development, Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, 2024. https://www.mlit.go.jp/en/toshi/kankyo/green_transformation.html

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces planning urban logistics facilities or depot locations in Japanese cities should be aware that the Urban Green Space Act creates new green-space quality and quantity requirements that may affect development permissions. This is an adjacent regulatory signal rather than a direct freight compliance obligation.

---

## Japan's GX Industrial Cluster Strategy — Relevant for Logistics Location Decisions

The GX2040 Vision explicitly addresses the geographic distribution of industrial activity in relation to decarbonised power sources. "Japan aims to build new industrial clusters by attracting corporate investments into locations with an abundance of clean energy such as decarbonised power sources." *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

*Analytical inference:* Freight forwarding operations serving Japanese manufacturing clients should monitor GX industrial cluster development, as the emergence of new clean-energy industrial zones will shift freight origin/destination patterns and create demand for new Japan domestic transport corridors. The MITI sector-specific investment strategy (Ver. 2, December 2024) maps budgeted support across 16 designated areas including electric vehicles, storage batteries, and offshore wind — each with distinct logistics demand profiles.

## Modal Shift Incentives in Japan — Logistics Budget FY2026

Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) approved a "staggering 8.28 billion JPY (approx. $58 million USD) budget for logistics efficiency in FY2026/25," representing "a 3.5x year-over-year increase in spending." This includes specific modal shift support: "Japan's budget explicitly targets 'modal shifts' (e.g., trucks to ferries/trains)." *Source: LogiShift — Japan's 2026 Logistics Budget: A Global Efficiency Blueprint, LogiShift, 26 December 2025. https://en.logishift.net/2025/12/26/japans-2026-logistics-budget-a-global-efficiency-blueprint/

*Analytical inference:* Modal shift from road to rail and coastal marine on Japan domestic freight corridors is being actively subsidised by MLIT. For workspaces moving high-value cargo in Japan on air-primary or road-primary modes, the modal shift incentive creates both a commercial opportunity (lower-cost or subsidised alternatives) and a competitive dynamic (carriers investing in modal-shift capabilities may offer GX-aligned services at competitive rates).

## Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) — Regional Decarbonisation Pathway

Japan is expanding GX efforts regionally. "The Southeast Asian countries have a common situation with Japan as they rely mostly on thermal power generation for power supply and have flourishing manufacturing industries. We will strengthen cooperation with them by working together through initiatives such as the Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC)." *Source: ANRE/METI — GX Policy article, 2025. https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/en/category/special/article/detail_214.html

*Analytical inference:* AZEC participation signals that Japan-origin clients with Southeast Asia supply chains may increasingly face GX-aligned procurement expectations across the full Asian logistics network, not only the Japan domestic segment. Workspaces active on Japan–Southeast Asia trade lanes should monitor whether AZEC produces freight-sector-specific standards or emissions reporting requirements.

## Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) — International Offset Pathway

*Analytical inference:* "Its Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) is a bilateral scheme to incentivise decarbonising technologies and mitigation actions in 31 partner countries. JCM credits are eligible for use in the GX-ETS." *Source: ICAP Japan GX-ETS factsheet, International Carbon Action Partnership, 2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces with freight operations in JCM partner countries may find alignment between transport-sector decarbonisation investments in those countries and JCM credit generation, though the JCM is primarily a bilateral investment mechanism rather than a direct credit-procurement marketplace for freight forwarders.

Provisional Translation The Basic Policy for the Realization of GX - A roadmap for the next 10 years - February 2023 1 1. Foreword Humanity is now facing a shared challenge of global climate change such as extreme weather and a rising number of massive natural disasters all over the world. As more countries and regions announce their net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions targets and the global momentum for decarbonization grows, Japan has made a global pledge for reducing GHG emissions by 46% in FY2030 and achieving net-zero GHG emissions by 2050, showing its strong national determination to combat climate change. Meanwhile, Russia’s military invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has dramatically changed the world’s energy situation. Every country has seen significant energy-related inflation. The situation in Japan is very tense as well. As electricity supply becomes stretched and energy prices soar, there is now a risk of the first full-scale energy crisis since the Oil Crisis of 1973. It goes without saying that ensuring stable energy supply is the foundation of citizens’ lives and business activities. The current crisis has revealed the vulnerabilities of Japan’s energy supply systems and their issues with regard to national energy security. For Japan, a country that has experienced many critical moments in history with stable energy supply being disrupted, the idea of Green Transformation, or GX, means a thorough overhaul of its post-war industrial/energy policies, as GX will transform our entire industrial and social structures centering around fossil energy sources, long established since the Industrial Revolution, into ones based on clean energy. As a result of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, European countries and the United States have further accelerated their existing decarbonization initiatives. They have launched national efforts to support investment leading to decarbonization in power generation, industry, and transportation sectors as well as residential sector for accelerated transition to a carbon-free society. The European Union has set a 140 trillion-yen target over 10 years for its joint public-private investment plan consisting of various support measures. Some European Union (EU) member countries have added extra measures worth several trillion yen. The U.S., in addition to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, introduced the Inflation Reduction Act in August 2022, with the aim of spending ¥50 trillion on energy and climate change over 10 years. These policies are examples of accelerated government-led efforts by European countries and the U.S. to support de- carbonization investment and to establish new markets and rules. Successful GX decarbonization investment is now the decisive factor for each business and state that wishes to remain competitive. As a country surrounded by sea and deprived of natural resources that can be extracted easily, Japan has traditionally focused on research and development in the field of decarbonization technologies, with Japanese corporations having technological strengths in many areas. Making the most of these technological advantages to accelerate GX will lead to the stable supply of energy as well as providing opportunities for putting Japan on track for a dramatic bounce-back to 2 economic growth. Japan’s economy needs to grow by leveraging the expertise and insight accumulated in the country’s private sector to support other countries’ effort for achieving net- zero GHG emissions, as well as creating new demand and markets in decarbonization business which will ultimately lead to reinforcing Japan’s industrial competitiveness. GX introduction can lead the way to clearing Japan’s global commitment of 46% reduction of GHG emissions in FY2030 and achieving net-zero GHG emissions by 2050.This initiative can also bring stable supply of inexpensive energy by reorganizing energy supply-demand structures, and furthermore, reforming Japan’s industrial and social structures, and building a society in which all citizens, including future generations, can live an affluent life. With these goals in mind, the GX Implementation Council, based on the results of its past discussions, has created the following policies for the initiatives to be undertaken for 10 years.1 Additionally, bills relevant to GX implementation will be submitted to the 211th session of the Diet. 1 These polices are based on the Sixth Strategic Energy Plan, Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures, and Japan's Long-term Strategy under the Paris Agreement, all decided by the Cabinet in October 2021, and summarize Japan’s global pledge for climate change actions (46% GHG reduction in FY2030 vs. FY2013 levels) as well as continuously trying to clear a higher goal of a 50% reduction in order to achieve net-zero GHG emissions by 2050) together with the country’s initiatives for strengthening its industrial competitiveness and developing its economy, among other undertakings. 3 2. Decarbonization initiatives towards GX based on the premise of ensuring a stable energy supply (1) Basic concept In response to the dire energy situation after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, European and North American countries, including the G7, have taken actions to maintain stable supply of energy in line with each country’s practical requirements. In addition to various measures that have been taken to address the issue of soaring energy retail prices, affected nations have been reaching out for an even wider introduction of renewable energy, as well as announcing policies for building more nuclear power plants, showing their enhanced moves towards ensuring stable energy supply. On the other hand, the development of a business environment under the electricity deregulation scheme has not gone smoothly inside Japan, together with developing a grid network for introducing renewable energy and also restarting nuclear power stations. The power shortage within Tokyo Electric Power Company and other companies' service areas in March and June 2022, coupled with soaring energy prices, have led to an energy crisis situation not experienced since the 1973 Oil Crisis. Stable supply of inexpensive energy is the very foundation of citizens’ daily lives as well as social and economic activities. As such, it is Japan’s top priority. Ensuring stable supply of energy is the fundamental prerequisite for both addressing climate change issues and facilitating GX over the coming years. At the same time, driving GX itself will lead to ensuring stable energy supply. In order to ensure stable supply of energy into the future, simply focusing on the retail prices of gasoline, kerosene, electricity, and gas as temporary actions to mitigate the impact of price volatility is not enough. Transition to a resilient energy supply-demand that can withstand an energy crisis is needed. To that end, promoting thorough energy efficiency improvement on the demand side and fuel switching within the manufacture will be facilitated to escape from excessive dependence on fossil energy sources. On the supply side, renewables, nuclear, and other power sources that contribute to national energy security and are highly effective for decarbonization will be used to their maximum potential, also in order to overcome the current crisis. Based on the understanding that the reconstruction of Fukushima is the starting point for promoting any energy policies, no efforts will be spared until Fukushima is rebuilt and reborn. Initiatives to that end include the decommissioning of Fukushima Dai-ichi Nuclear Power Station, lifting of evacuation orders in Difficult-to-Return Zones, creating new businesses through the Fukushima Innovation Coast Framework, and revitalizing local businesses and livelihoods. Furthermore, the fundamental premise for utilizing nuclear power is that we will never forget the 4 lessons learned from the accident and give top priority to safety in nuclear power while being free of safety myths. GX implementation has many requirements. The initiative will leverage Japanese companies’ globally acclaimed technologies for decarbonization to help worldwide efforts aimed at achieving net-zero GHG emissions. Furthermore, by creating new markets and demands as well as strengthening Japan’s industrial competitiveness, the country’s economy can be put back on track for further growth, leading to future economic development and growth in jobs and income. These basic concepts and discussions in the GX Implementation Council meetings form the foundation of the following initiatives. (2) Next steps2 1) Promotion of thorough energy efficiency improvement and restructuring the manufacturing industry (through fuel and feedstocks transition) Energy efficiency improvement not only contributes to a decarbonized society through reducing energy consumption but also building an energy supply-demand structure that is resilient to crises. As such, we will promote bold energy efficiency improvement through a combination of regulatory measures and support measures based on "the Act on the Rationalizing Energy Use and Shifting to Non-fossil Energy” For companies, we will strengthen the support measures for SMEs by subsidies which are eligible for multiple-year investment plans. We will also strengthen the support measures for small business owners by increasing subsidies for energy efficiency diagnosis, which examines the use of energy and suggests how to improve energy efficiency. 2 The Sixth Strategic Energy Plan decided by the Cabinet in October 2021 states that, based on the assumption that ensuring stable supply of inexpensive energy is vital not only for maintaining and strengthening Japan’s vitality but also for a 46% GHG reduction in FY2030 and achieving net-zero GHG emissions by 2050, “Japan will address maximum introduction of renewable energy as major power sources as the top priority; societal implementation of hydrogen and Carbon dioxide Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) will be promoted; and a necessary amount of nuclear power will be continuously utilized on the major premise of ensuring safety and public trust. Including these efforts, Japan will pursue all options to realize net-zero GHG emissions by 2050 by striving to maintain global competitiveness and to restrain the citizens’ burden by securing a stable and cost-efficient energy supply.” The Sixth Strategic Energy Plan has made clear that Japan’s fundamental energy strategy for clearing the ambitious goal of achieving net-zero GHG emissions by 2050 must be built by considering all possibilities and utilizing all available technologies. All the actions listed in this document for ensuring stable supply of energy are within the guidelines set by this Sixth Strategic Energy Plan, aiming to define all options based on these guidelines. 5 For the households, relevant ministries and agencies will work together to facilitate spontaneous cooperation and initiatives by citizens by, for example, establishing a single point of contact and strengthening one-stop support for the existing programs to support energy efficiency retrofitting in houses, such as replacing windows with thermal insulated models with higher energy efficiency performance. At the same time, relevant authorities will promote the understanding between consumers for energy efficiency improvement and changes in consumer behavior so that the effort take root as a comfortable lifestyles. Special Cash Payments for Resident Tax-Exempted Households, Etc. will be utilized to back up initiatives by municipalities, taking local needs into account, to support replacing appliances with energy efficient ones. Based on "the Act on the Rationalizing Energy Use and Shifting to Non-fossil Energy”, large- scale consumers are obliged to submit their medium- and long-term plans and periodic reports on the shift to non-fossil energy. We will encourage the shift to non-fossil fuel energy with newly proposed governmental guidelines for the five key industries (iron and steel, chemical, cement manufacturing, paper manufacturing, and automotive manufacturing) that use 40% of energy consumed by the entire industry sector3. In addition, by introducing a new system of voluntary disclosure of the periodic report information under the Act, we will encourage companies to disclose information about energy efficiency improvement and shift to non-fossil energy.
